subject: maths
title: Primary 4 Factors and Multiples
seo_title: P4 Factors and Multiples Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Factors and multiples; common factors of two numbers; common multiples of two 1-digit numbers
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice: factors, factor pairs, common factors, multiples, common multiples and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A factor divides a number exactly. A multiple is the number times 1, 2, 3, …
key_sub: 12 = 3 × 4, so 3 and 4 are factors of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 3 and of 4.
body_html:
Factors

A factor of a number divides it exactly, with no remainder. 12 = 3 × 4, so 3 and 4 are factors of 12.

To find all the factors, find the factor pairs. Start with 1 × the number. Try 2, 3, 4, … and stop when the pairs start to repeat.

Example

Find all the factors of 18.

Factor pairs: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. 4 and 5 do not divide 18. The next pair, 6 × 3, repeats.

Answer: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18

Is it a factor? Divide. If there is no remainder, it is a factor. 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so 8 is a factor of 56. 56 ÷ 6 = 9 R 2, so 6 is not.

Common factors

A common factor is a factor of both numbers. List the factors of each number and circle the numbers in both lists. 1 is always a common factor.

Multiples

The multiples of a number are the number × 1, × 2, × 3, … The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, … The first multiple is the number itself.

Factors and multiples go together: 3 is a factor of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 3. A factor is never bigger than the number. A multiple is never smaller.

Common multiples

A common multiple is a multiple of both numbers. Count in the bigger number and stop at the first number that the smaller number also divides.

Example

Buns come in packets of 6 and sausages in packets of 8. What is the least number of each to buy so there are the same number of buns and sausages?

Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24. 24 is a multiple of 6 too. In the model, 4 packets of buns and 3 packets of sausages are the same length.

Answer: 24 buns and 24 sausages

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting 1 and the number itself: “the factors of 15 are 3 and 5”Start with 1 × 15: the factors are 1, 3, 5, 15
Mixing up factors and multiples: “4 is a multiple of 12”4 is a factor of 12. 12 is a multiple of 4
Listing only one common factor: “the common factor of 20 and 30 is 10”List them all: 1, 2, 5, 10
Thinking every even number has 4 as a factor30 ÷ 4 = 7 R 2, so 4 is not a factor of 30
Multiplying for the first common multiple: 4 × 6 = 24Count in 6s: 6, 12. 12 comes first

faq.q: What is taught in P4 factors and multiples?
faq.a: Primary 4 students find all the factors of a number, check whether a number is a factor, find common factors of two numbers, list multiples and find common multiples of two 1-digit numbers. They use these ideas in word problems about packets, groups and bus timings.

faq.q: How do I explain factors and multiples to my child?
faq.a: Use an example like 3 × 4 = 12: 3 and 4 are factors of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 3 and of 4. Factors are the numbers you multiply; the multiple is the answer.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with factors and multiples?
faq.a: The most common mistake is forgetting 1 and the number itself when listing factors. Many children also mix up factors and multiples, or give only one common factor when the question asks for all of them.

faq.q: Is factors and multiples in the MOE Primary 4 syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Factors and multiples, common factors of two numbers and common multiples of two 1-digit numbers are part of Whole Numbers in the MOE 2021 Primary 4 Mathematics syllabus. These skills are used later in fractions, and in the PSLE.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 12?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. So the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Do not forget 1 and 12, and do not leave out the pair 3 × 4. 12, 24, 36, 48 are multiples of 12, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 18?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. So the factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Do not forget 1 and 18, and do not leave out the pair 3 × 6. 18, 36, 54, 72 are multiples of 18, not factors.

items.q: How many factors does 16 have?
items.e: The factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16. That is 5 factors. 4 × 4 = 16, so 4 is counted only once. Counting 4 twice gives 6, leaving out 1 and 16 gives 3, and leaving out 16 gives 4.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 20?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5. So the factors of 20 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Do not forget 1 and 20, and do not leave out the pair 4 × 5. 20, 40, 60, 80 are multiples of 20, not factors.

items.q: How many factors does 24 have?
items.e: The factor pairs are 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6, so 24 has 8 factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. 4 is the number of pairs. Leaving out 1 and 24 gives 6, and leaving out 24 gives 7.

items.q: This array has 18 counters. Which factor pair of 18 does it show?
items.e: Count the rows and the counters in each row: 3 rows of 6. So the array shows 3 × 6 = 18. 2 × 9 is also a factor pair of 18, but it is not this array.

items.q: This array has 20 counters. Which factor pair of 20 does it show?
items.e: Count the rows and the counters in each row: 4 rows of 5. So the array shows 4 × 5 = 20. 2 × 10 is also a factor pair of 20, but it is not this array.

items.q: This array has 36 counters. Which factor pair of 36 does it show?
items.e: Count the rows and the counters in each row: 4 rows of 9. So the array shows 4 × 9 = 36. 6 × 6 is also a factor pair of 36, but it is not this array.

items.q: These are the factor pairs of 30: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, ? × 6. What is the missing number?
items.e: 6 × 5 = 30, so the missing number is 5. 4 × 6 = 24 and 3 × 6 = 18. 24 is 30 − 6: we multiply, not subtract.

items.q: Which of these is a factor pair of 42?
Mrs Lim puts 12 chairs in equal rows. Which of these is not possible?
items.e: 12 ÷ 5 = 2 R 2, so 5 rows is not possible: 5 is not a factor of 12. 2 rows of 6, 3 rows of 4 and 1 row of 12 all work.

items.q: Kumar puts 24 stamps on a page in equal rows. Which number of rows is not possible?
items.e: 24 ÷ 5 = 4 R 4, so 5 rows is not possible. 3 rows of 8, 4 rows of 6 and 6 rows of 4 all work.

items.q: These are the factor pairs of 36: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × ?, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. What is the missing number?
items.e: 3 × 12 = 36, so the missing number is 12. 3 × 11 = 33 and 3 × 13 = 39. 33 is 36 − 3: we multiply, not subtract.

items.q: These are the factor pairs of 40: 1 × 40, 2 × 20, 4 × ?, 5 × 8. What is the missing number?
items.e: 4 × 10 = 40, so the missing number is 10. 36 is 40 − 4: we multiply, not subtract. 20 is already in the pair 2 × 20, and 4 × 9 = 36.

items.q: Which number is a factor of every whole number?
items.e: Every number can be written as 1 × itself, for example 7 = 1 × 7. So 1 is a factor of every number. 2 is not a factor of odd numbers, and 10 is not a factor of 7.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 30?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. So the factors of 30 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Do not forget 1 and 30, and do not leave out the pair 5 × 6. 30, 60, 90, 120 are multiples of 30, not factors.

items.q: What is the greatest factor of 45?
items.e: 45 = 1 × 45, so the greatest factor of 45 is 45 itself. 15 is the next greatest factor. 90 is a multiple of 45, not a factor. A factor is never greater than the number.

items.q: Ali says the factors of 15 are 3 and 5. Is he right?
items.e: 15 = 1 × 15 and 15 = 3 × 5, so the factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5 and 15. Ali forgot 1 and 15. 30 is a multiple of 15, and 15 ÷ 2 = 7 R 1.

items.q: Siti lists the factors of 28: 1, 2, 4, 14, 28. Which factor is missing?
items.e: The factor pairs of 28 are 1 × 28, 2 × 14 and 4 × 7. Siti has 4 but not its partner, 7. 28 ÷ 3 and 28 ÷ 6 have remainders, and 56 is a multiple of 28.

items.q: Which list shows all the factor pairs of 18?
items.e: Try 1, 2, 3, … in order: 1 × 18, 2 × 9 and 3 × 6. 4 and 5 are not factors of 18 (4 × 5 = 20). So the answer is 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. Do not leave out 1 × 18.

items.q: Which number has 5 as a factor?
items.e: 85 ÷ 5 = 17, so 5 is a factor of 85. Numbers with 5 as a factor end in 0 or 5. 58, 52 and 57 do not.

items.q: 42 counters are put into groups of 6. What does the picture show?
items.e: There are 7 groups of 6 and none left over: 42 ÷ 6 = 7. So 6 is a factor of 42 (and 7 is too). 42 is a multiple of 6, not a factor of 6.

items.q: 26 counters are put into groups of 4. What does the picture show?
items.e: There are 6 groups of 4 and 2 left over: 26 ÷ 4 = 6 R 2. A remainder means 4 is not a factor of 26, and 26 is not a multiple of 4. 2 is a factor of 26 (26 ÷ 2 = 13).

items.q: Which number is a factor of 48?
items.e: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, so 6 is a factor of 48. 48 ÷ 5 = 9 R 3, 48 ÷ 7 = 6 R 6, 48 ÷ 9 = 5 R 3. A remainder means it is not a factor.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 63?
items.e: 63 ÷ 9 = 7, so 9 is a factor of 63. 63 ÷ 4 = 15 R 3, 63 ÷ 6 = 10 R 3, 63 ÷ 8 = 7 R 7. A remainder means it is not a factor.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 45?
items.e: 45 ÷ 5 = 9, so 5 is a factor of 45. 45 ÷ 2 = 22 R 1, 45 ÷ 4 = 11 R 1, 45 ÷ 7 = 6 R 3. A remainder means it is not a factor.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 56?
items.e: 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so 8 is a factor of 56. 56 ÷ 3 = 18 R 2, 56 ÷ 5 = 11 R 1, 56 ÷ 6 = 9 R 2. A remainder means it is not a factor.

items.q: Is 6 a factor of 34?
items.e: 6 × 5 = 30 and 6 × 6 = 36, so 34 ÷ 6 = 5 R 4. There is a remainder, so 6 is not a factor of 34. Being even only tells us 2 is a factor.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 60?
Which number is not a factor of 84?
Which number is not a factor of 90?
Which number is not a factor of 72?
9 is a factor of which number?
items.e: 9 × 9 = 81, so 9 is a factor of 81. 79 ÷ 9 = 8 R 7, 91 ÷ 9 = 10 R 1 and 89 ÷ 9 = 9 R 8. The last digit does not tell you.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 8 × 8 = 64, so 8 is a factor of 64. 60 ÷ 8 = 7 R 4 and 64 ÷ 6 = 10 R 4. 64 is a multiple of 8, not a factor of 8.

items.q: Which of these numbers has 4 as a factor?
items.e: 52 ÷ 4 = 13, so 4 is a factor of 52. 42, 54 and 46 are even, but each leaves a remainder 2 when divided by 4. Even does not mean 4 is a factor.

items.q: Which number has both 3 and 4 as factors?
items.e: 36 = 3 × 12 and 36 = 4 × 9, so 36 has both. 32 has 4 but not 3, 27 has 3 but not 4, and 34 has neither: 34 ÷ 3 = 11 R 1 and 34 ÷ 4 = 8 R 2.

items.q: Which division has no remainder?
How many of the numbers 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are factors of 30?
Raju says 4 is a factor of 30 because 30 is even. Is he right?
items.e: 4 × 7 = 28 and 4 × 8 = 32, so 30 ÷ 4 = 7 R 2. 4 is not a factor of 30. Even numbers have 2 as a factor, but not always 4.

items.q: Which number between 50 and 60 has 7 as a factor?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, so the answer is 56. 57 ends in 7, but 57 ÷ 7 = 8 R 1. 54 ÷ 7 = 7 R 5 and 58 ÷ 7 = 8 R 2.

items.q: The common factors of 12 and 18 are circled. Which list shows all the common factors?
items.e: The circled numbers are in both rows, so the common factors are 1, 2, 3, 6. Do not forget 1, and list every common factor, not only the greatest one.

items.q: The common factors of 16 and 24 are circled. Which list shows all the common factors?
items.e: The circled numbers are in both rows, so the common factors are 1, 2, 4, 8. Do not forget 1, and list every common factor, not only the greatest one.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 8 and 12?
items.e: Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4. Remember 1 is always a common factor, and list them all.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 20 and 30?
items.e: Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 5, 10. Remember 1 is always a common factor, and list them all.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 15 and 25?
items.e: Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. Factors of 25: 1, 5, 25. The numbers in both lists are 1, 5. Remember 1 is always a common factor, and list them all.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 18 and 27?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. The numbers in both lists are 1, 3, 9. Remember 1 is always a common factor, and list them all.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 24 and 36?
items.e: 24 = 4 × 6 and 36 = 4 × 9, so 4 is a common factor. 8 is a factor of 24 only, and 9 is a factor of 36 only. 72 is a common multiple, not a factor.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 30 and 45?
items.e: 30 = 5 × 6 and 45 = 5 × 9, so 5 is a common factor. 6 is a factor of 30 only, and 9 is a factor of 45 only. 90 is a common multiple, not a factor.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 28 and 42?
items.e: 28 = 7 × 4 and 42 = 7 × 6, so 7 is a common factor. 4 is a factor of 28 only, and 6 is a factor of 42 only. 84 is a common multiple, not a factor.

items.q: Priya says the only common factor of 20 and 30 is 10. Is she right?
c: No. 1 and 10 are the only ones
No. 60 is a common factor too
items.e: Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 5, 10. 10 is the greatest, but there are 4 common factors. 60 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 18 and 30?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 3, 6. 9 is a factor of 18, but 30 ÷ 9 = 3 R 3, so 9 is not a common factor.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 24 and 40?
items.e: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4, 8. 3 is a factor of 24, but 40 ÷ 3 = 13 R 1, so 3 is not a common factor.

items.q: How many common factors do 12 and 30 have?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 3, 6. That is 4 common factors. Leaving out 1 gives 3. 6 is the greatest one, not how many.

items.q: How many common factors do 20 and 28 have?
items.e: Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Factors of 28: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4. That is 3 common factors. Leaving out 1 gives 2. 4 is the greatest one, and 6 is how many factors 20 has.

items.q: What is the greatest number that is a factor of both 12 and 20?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4. The greatest is 4. 2 is a common factor, but not the greatest. 60 is a common multiple, and 12 is not a factor of 20.

items.q: What is the greatest number that is a factor of both 18 and 24?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 3, 6. The greatest is 6. 3 and 2 are common factors too, but smaller. 72 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which two numbers have 6 as a common factor?
items.e: 12 = 6 × 2 and 18 = 6 × 3, so 6 is a common factor of 12 and 18. 15 ÷ 6 = 2 R 3, 6 is not a factor of 3, and 16 and 26 only end in 6.

items.q: Which two numbers have only 1 as a common factor?
items.e: Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Only 1 is in both, so the answer is 8 and 9. 6 and 9 share 3, 4 and 10 share 2, and 9 and 12 share 3.

items.q: Jun Jie says the common factors of 12 and 16 are 2 and 4. Which common factor did he miss?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4. Jun Jie missed 1. 8 is a factor of 16 only, 3 is a factor of 12 only, and 48 is a common multiple.

items.q: Is 4 a common factor of 28 and 36?
c: No. 4 is a factor of 28 only
No. 4 is a factor of 36 only
items.e: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 and 36 ÷ 4 = 9 with no remainders, so 4 is a common factor of 28 and 36.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 6?
items.e: Multiply 6 by 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. The first multiple of a number is the number itself, not 0. Count on in 6s, not in 10s. 1, 2, 3, 6 are the factors of 6, not multiples.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 7?
items.e: Multiply 7 by 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. The first multiple of a number is the number itself, not 0. Count on in 7s, not in 10s. 27 is not a multiple of 7 (7 × 4 = 28).

items.q: The jumps are all the same size. What number is at ?
items.e: Count on in 4s from 0: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40. The missing number is 28 (4 × 7).

items.q: The jumps are all the same size. What number is at ?
items.e: Count on in 9s from 0: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54. The missing number is 36 (9 × 4).

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 6?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42, so 42 is a multiple of 6. 3 is a factor of 6, not a multiple. 46 ÷ 6 = 7 R 4 and 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4. Ending in 6 does not make a number a multiple of 6.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 8?
items.e: 8 × 8 = 64, so 64 is a multiple of 8. 4 is a factor of 8, not a multiple. 68 ÷ 8 = 8 R 4 and 60 ÷ 8 = 7 R 4. Ending in 8 does not make a number a multiple of 8.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 9?
items.e: 9 × 6 = 54, so 54 is a multiple of 9. 3 is a factor of 9, not a multiple. 59 ÷ 9 = 6 R 5 and 49 ÷ 9 = 5 R 4. Ending in 9 does not make a number a multiple of 9.

items.q: Which number is not a multiple of 7?
Which number is not a multiple of 4?
items.e: 34 ÷ 4 = 8 R 2, so 34 is not a multiple of 4. 24 = 4 × 6, 36 = 4 × 9 and 48 = 4 × 12. 34 is even, but that is not enough.

items.q: What is the 8th multiple of 6?
items.e: The 8th multiple of 6 is 6 × 8 = 48. 42 is the 7th multiple and 54 is the 9th. 14 is 6 + 8: we multiply, not add.

items.q: What is the 10th multiple of 9?
items.e: The 10th multiple of 9 is 9 × 10 = 90. 81 is the 9th multiple and 99 is the 11th. 19 is 9 + 10.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36, so 36 is a multiple of 9, and 9 is a factor of 36. A multiple is never smaller than the number. A factor is never bigger.

items.q: Ahmad says 4 is a multiple of 12 because 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Is he right?
items.e: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 with no remainder, so 4 is a factor of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 4. The multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, … They are never smaller than 12.

items.q: What is the smallest multiple of 7 that is greater than 50?
items.e: 7 × 7 = 49 and 7 × 8 = 56. 49 is less than 50, so the answer is 56. 57 ends in 7, but 57 ÷ 7 = 8 R 1. 63 is a multiple of 7, but not the smallest one after 50.

items.q: How many multiples of 6 are there between 20 and 50?
items.e: Count in 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54. Five of them are between 20 and 50. Do not leave out 48, and do not count 18 or 54.

items.q: Is 8 a multiple of 8?
c: No. A multiple must be bigger
No. 8 is only a factor of 8
items.e: 8 × 1 = 8, so 8 is the first multiple of 8. Every number is a multiple of itself, and also a factor of itself.

items.q: Zhi Hao counts in 8s: 8, 16, 24, 30, 40. Which number is wrong?
items.e: 8 × 4 = 32, so the 4th number should be 32, not 30. 16 = 8 × 2, 24 = 8 × 3 and 40 = 8 × 5.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 5 but not a multiple of 10?
items.e: Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. Multiples of 10 end in 0. So 35 is a multiple of 5 but not of 10. 50 and 30 are multiples of both, and 53 is not a multiple of 5.

items.q: Hui Min counts in 7s from 7. Will she say 46?
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42 and 7 × 7 = 49. 46 is between them, so 46 is not a multiple of 7. Being even is not the reason: 42 is even and is a multiple of 7.

items.q: Which list has only multiples of 9?
items.e: 18 = 9 × 2, 36 = 9 × 4, 54 = 9 × 6 and 72 = 9 × 8, so the answer is 18, 36, 54, 72. 19, 29 and 39 only end in 9. 1, 3 and 9 are the factors of 9. 46 is not a multiple of 9.

items.q: Which numbers in the picture are common multiples of 4 and 6?
items.e: Look for numbers in both rows. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. The common multiples are 12, 24, 36. Not only 4 × 6 = 24, and not only the first one.

items.q: Use the picture. What is the first common multiple of 3 and 5?
items.e: The first number in both rows is 15. 30 is a common multiple too, but not the first. 8 is 3 + 5, and 5 is a multiple of 5 only.

items.q: Which list shows the first three common multiples of 6 and 9?
items.e: Count in 9s: 9, 18. 18 = 6 × 3, so the first common multiple is 18. Then count in 18s: 18, 36, 54. 6 × 9 = 54 is a common multiple, but not the first. 9 and 27 are not multiples of 6.

items.q: What is the first common multiple of 6 and 8?
items.e: Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24. The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 24. 6 × 8 = 48 is a common multiple, but not the first. 14 is 6 + 8. 16 is a multiple of 8 only.

items.q: What is the first common multiple of 4 and 8?
items.e: 8 = 4 × 2, so 8 is already a multiple of 4. The first common multiple is 8. When one number is a multiple of the other, the bigger number is the first common multiple. 4 × 8 = 32 is a common multiple, but not the first. 12 is 4 + 8. 16 is a common multiple, but not the first.

items.q: What is the first common multiple of 4 and 5?
items.e: Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. The first one that is also a multiple of 4 is 20. 40 is a common multiple, but not the first. 9 is 4 + 5. 10 is a multiple of 5 only.

items.q: Which number is a common multiple of 4 and 6?
items.e: 36 = 4 × 9 and 36 = 6 × 6, so 36 is a common multiple. 16 is a multiple of 4 only, 18 is a multiple of 6 only, and 10 is 4 + 6.

items.q: Buns come in packets of 6 and sausages in packets of 8. Ethan wants the same number of buns and sausages for a barbecue at East Coast Park. What is the least number of each he can buy?
items.e: Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24. The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 24. The two bars are the same length at 24: 4 packets of buns and 3 packets of sausages. 6 × 8 = 48 also works, but it is not the least. 14 is 6 + 8, and 12 is not a multiple of 8.

items.q: Buns come in packets of 6 and sausages in packets of 8. Mei Ling buys the least number of packets so that she has the same number of buns and sausages. How many packets of buns does she buy?
items.e: The first common multiple of 6 and 8 is 24, so she needs 24 buns: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 packets. 3 packets is for the sausages (24 ÷ 8). 24 is the number of buns, not packets.

items.q: At a bus interchange, Bus A leaves every 6 minutes and Bus B leaves every 8 minutes. Both buses leave at 7.00 am. When will they next leave at the same time?
items.e: Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24. The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 24. So they leave together again 24 min later, at 7.24 am. 7.48 am uses 6 × 8 = 48 min, 7.14 am uses 6 + 8 = 14 min, and at 7.08 am only Bus B leaves.

items.q: Bus 12 leaves a stop every 5 minutes and Bus 21 leaves every 6 minutes. Both leave together at 3.30 pm. When will they next leave together?
items.e: Count in 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. The first one that is also a multiple of 5 is 30. 30 min after 3.30 pm is 4.00 pm. 3.41 pm uses 5 + 6 = 11 min. At 3.36 pm only Bus 21 leaves, and at 3.35 pm only Bus 12 leaves.

items.q: At Gardens by the Bay, a red light flashes every 4 seconds and a blue light flashes every 6 seconds. They flash together now. After how many seconds will they next flash together?
items.e: Count in 6s: 6, 12. The first one that is also a multiple of 4 is 12. So they flash together after 12 s. 24 s is 4 × 6: a common multiple, but not the first. 10 s is 4 + 6, and 2 is a common factor.

items.q: Siti stacks blocks that are each 6 cm tall. Hafiz stacks blocks that are each 9 cm tall. Their towers are the same height. What is the smallest possible height?
items.e: Count in 9s: 9, 18. The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 18. The towers are both 18 cm: 3 blocks for Siti and 2 for Hafiz. 54 cm (6 × 9) and 36 cm are also the same height, but not the smallest. 15 cm is 6 + 9.

items.q: Nurul has swimming every 4 days and art lessons every 6 days. She has both on 3 March. On what date will she next have both?
items.e: Count in 6s: 6, 12. The first one that is also a multiple of 4 is 12. 3 March + 12 days = 15 March. 27 March uses 4 × 6 = 24 days, 13 March uses 4 + 6 = 10 days, and 5 March uses 2 days (a common factor).

items.q: Mrs Ng has some sweets. She can share them equally among 6 children or among 8 children, with none left over. What is the smallest number of sweets she can have?
items.e: The number of sweets must be a multiple of 6 and of 8. Count in 8s: 8, 16, 24. The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 24. 48 also works, but it is not the smallest. 14 is 6 + 8, and 2 is a common factor.

items.q: The P4 students can be put into groups of 4 or groups of 9 with no one left out. There are fewer than 50 students. How many students are there?
items.e: The number must be a common multiple of 4 and 9. Count in 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45. 36 = 4 × 9 is the only one less than 50 that is also a multiple of 4. 45 and 40 are multiples of one number only, and 13 is 4 + 9.

items.q: Mr Rahman has 18 apples and 24 oranges. He packs them into bags. Every bag has the same number of apples and the same number of oranges, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags?
items.e: The number of bags must be a common factor of 18 and 24: 1, 2, 3 and 6. The greatest is 6, so each bag has 3 apples and 4 oranges. 3 and 2 also work, but they are not the greatest. 72 is a common multiple.

items.q: Kavya has 12 red beads and 20 blue beads. She makes bracelets that are all the same and uses every bead. Which of these could be the number of bracelets?
items.e: The number of bracelets must be a common factor of 12 and 20 (1, 2 or 4). Of these choices, only 4 bracelets works, each with 3 red and 5 blue beads. 3 and 6 are factors of 12 only, and 5 is a factor of 20 only.

items.q: Paper cups come in packs of 4 and paper plates in packs of 6. Wei Ming says he must buy 24 of each to have the same number. Is he right?
items.e: Count in 6s: 6, 12. The first one that is also a multiple of 4 is 12. The model shows 3 packs of cups and 2 packs of plates give 12 of each. 24 also works, but it is not the least. 10 is 4 + 6, and 2 is a common factor.

items.q: A bubble tea shop gives a free sticker to every 6th customer and a free keychain to every 9th customer. Which customer is the first to get both?
items.e: Count in 9s: 9, 18. The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 18. So the 18th customer is the first to get both. 54 is 6 × 9, 15 is 6 + 9, and 3 is a common factor.
